title: Game Night
cn: 第 15 集 · 游戏之夜
novel:
Lily invented a board game in which every player must [[reveal|reveal]] one story they have never told.

They threw the [[dice|dice]]. Each [[opponent|opponent]] became [[ruthless|ruthless]]. Barney tried to [[cheat|cheat]] within four minutes.

Marshall went first and told a story so [[hilarious|hilarious]] that Lily nearly fell off her chair. Robin then admitted a small [[scandal|scandal]] from her school days, and everyone began to [[tease|tease]] her until she started to [[blush|blush]].

Barney did not [[exaggerate|exaggerate]] for once. He said nothing at all, which was worse.

The [[rivalry|rivalry]] turned [[brutal|brutal]]. There was [[gossip|gossip]]. There was a [[bet|bet]]. Somebody made a private [[wager|wager]] about who would [[spill the beans|spill the beans]] first.

Then it was Ted's turn, and the room went quiet. He had spent years trying to [[cover up|cover up]] one very stupid year of his life. His [[reputation|reputation]] as the sensible one depended on it.

He told the truth.

Nobody [[mocked|mock]] him. Nobody [[judged|judge]] him. His friends did not [[betray|betray]] the secret, and by the end of the night they had all decided to [[forgive|forgive]] each other's past — mostly because everyone's past was equally [[shameful|shameful]].

reveal.en: to tell people something that was secret

dice.en: small cubes with dots, thrown in games

opponent.en: the person you play or fight against

ruthless.en: hard and cruel; not caring about others' feelings

cheat.en: to break the rules secretly to win

scandal.en: a shocking story that makes people talk badly about someone

tease.en: to laugh at someone in a friendly or unkind way

blush.en: to become red in the face because you feel shy

exaggerate.en: to say something is bigger or better than it really is

rivalry.en: when two people always try to beat each other

gossip.en: talk about other people's private lives

bet.en: an agreement to pay money if you guess wrong

wager.en: a more formal word for a bet

spill the beans.en: to tell a secret by accident

cover up.en: to hide something bad so nobody finds out

reputation.en: what people generally think about you

mock.en: to laugh at someone in an unkind way

judge.en: to decide that someone is bad or wrong

betray.en: to hurt someone who trusts you, for example by telling their secret

forgive.en: to stop being angry with someone

shameful.en: so bad that you should feel ashamed
